text: Hunter Schafer, born December 31, 1998, in Trenton, New Jersey, and raised in Raleigh, North Carolina, is an American actress, model, and activist. Her father was a pastor, and the family moved between churches in New Jersey, Arizona, and eventually Raleigh, where Schafer grew up. She has three younger siblings: two sisters and a brother. Schafer began expressing femininity as a toddler; in seventh grade, she came out to her parents as a gay boy, but developed gender dysphoria in eighth grade and came out as a transgender girl in ninth grade, beginning her transition after being diagnosed with dysphoria. She also questioned whether she had a non-binary identity and found support through YouTube and social media. In 2016, she became the youngest plaintiff in the ACLU and Lambda Legal lawsuit Carcaño v. McCrory against North Carolina's Public Facilities Privacy & Security Act, a "bathroom bill" that prohibited transgender people from using bathrooms matching their gender identity. The lawsuit led to the bill's repeal, and Schafer made a film protesting it released by Rookie and wrote an essay for Teen Vogue in July 2016. For her activism, she was named to Teen Vogue's "21 Under 21" list in 2017 and granted an interview with Hillary Clinton. Schafer studied watercolor painting and clothing design; she designed clothes in high school, inspired by Tim Burton and Skottie Young, and posted her artwork on Instagram, which gained popularity. Her designs, often featuring political messaging, were featured by Huffington Post in 2017. She attended Needham B. Broughton High School and transferred to the North Carolina School of the Arts, graduating from its visual arts program. In 2017, she was a semifinalist in the U.S. Presidential Scholars Program. After high school, she planned to attend Central Saint Martins in London to study clothing design for nonbinary people and intended to open a studio and gallery for trans artists using grant money from Teen Vogue. She signed with Elite Model Management in 2017 after meeting an agent on Instagram and moved to Brooklyn to model in New York City, working with brands such as Dior, Marc Jacobs, Converse, Gucci, Helmut Lang, Versus, and Versace. She walked for nine fashion houses in early 2018, made her debut at New York Fashion Week, and traveled to Europe. Marie Claire praised her for her ethereal yet edgy look and versatility. In 2019, she was cast in the HBO series Euphoria as transgender high school student Jules Vaughn, after finding a casting call on Instagram requiring no prior acting experience. She completed her final audition in Los Angeles, filmed the pilot there, and moved to Los Angeles to film the first season. At the time, trans television characters and trans actors in such roles were rare. She worked with creator Sam Levinson and costume designer Heidi Bivens to ensure Jules's experiences were accurate and was praised by Vulture for not being a passive victim of violence. Her performance was widely acclaimed, earning her a Shorty Award, an MTV Movie & TV Award, and a Dorian Award. The Advocate noted she should have been nominated at the 2020 Primetime Emmy Awards, and Queerty named her one of 50 queer people leading toward equality in 2020. In 2021, she co-wrote the Euphoria episode "Fuck Anyone Who's Not a Sea Blob," which featured Jules in therapy and was critically acclaimed. In 2020, she became the global brand ambassador for Shiseido Makeup; in 2021, Prada named her their new house ambassador, and Time included her on its Next list of emerging leaders, with a tribute by Euphoria co-star Zendaya. In 2022, she starred in the English dub of the Japanese film Belle and made her directorial debut with the music video for Girl in Red's song "hornylovesickmess," sharing storyboard sketches with the final shots. She directed the music video for Anohni and the Johnsons' "Why Am I Alive Now?" in 2023 and became the new face of Mugler's Angel perfume. She starred in The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes (2023) as Tigris Snow, a role praised as "excellent" and "underused," with director Francis Lawrence citing her disarming authenticity and warm audition. She continued modeling for Alexander McQueen, Prada, and Schiaparelli. At the 2023 Vanity Fair after-party for the 95th Academy Awards, she wore a white maxi skirt and a top with a horizontal feather covering her nipples, designed by Ludovic de Saint Sernin for Ann Demeulemeester, an outfit that became infamous and sparked widespread discussion, later referenced by Spanish pop singer Rosalía in a 2025 photoshoot. Since the Songbirds & Snakes press tour, she has been stylized by Dara Allen, whom she considers a close friend, and some attribute her fashion success to their collaboration. In 2024, she starred in Tilman Singer's horror film Cuckoo, her first lead role in a feature film, which she described as "the training wheels" turning off and which received praise for its "intense and emotional central performance"; she also appeared in a scene in Yorgos Lanthimos's anthology film Kinds of Kindness. In 2025, she starred in the horror short film The Hunt, directed by Nadia Lee Cohen, to promote Gentle Monster's autumn 2025 campaign. In 2025, a leaker reported she was initially considered for the role of Princess Zelda in the live-action The Legend of Zelda film, which was later given to Bo Bragason; the rumor sparked both supportive and transphobic reactions, with some outlets speculating Nintendo chose a cisgender woman to avoid backlash, though this has not been confirmed. Schafer has upcoming roles in David Lowery's Mother Mary, Tom Ford's Cry to Heaven, Zach Strauss' Palette, Hideo Kojima's horror video game OD, the Amazon series Blade Runner 2099, and a horror film by Arkasha Stevenson. In 2019, she identified as closer to a lesbian, and in 2021, described herself as bi or pan or something. She had a brief relationship with Rosalía from 2019 to 2020, which she confirmed in 2024, and considers her "family no matter what"; she dated Euphoria co-star Dominic Fike from February 2022 to around July 2023, ending the relationship after discovering he cheated. In 2019, she used she/her pronouns and the title "Mx. Schafer," stating in 2016 that she was not a cis girl. In 2024, she said she wanted to talk less about her trans identity as she had moved past the most difficult parts of her transition and no longer wanted to be seen solely as a "trans starlet," declining many trans roles. In an interview with Rolling Stone, she said, "No. I'm just a tranny who's famous, you know?" and in a 2024 Vogue interview, she discussed balancing visibility and responsibility in representation, saying she constantly "does the math of when to reel it in and when to lean into it." In 2022, she liked and commented "!!!!!" on an Instagram post criticizing certain non-binary activists who opposed trans identities being considered a medical condition requiring dysphoria, linking such activism to anti-trans legislation; this drew backlash from some fans, who accused her of endorsing transmedicalism, which she denied, stating she believed there was an imbalance in visibility between non-binary people and binary trans women, especially those of color or who rely on sex work, and that this deserved attention. On February 27, 2024, Schafer and fifty others were arrested in New York City during a Jewish Voice for Peace protest outside 30 Rockefeller Center, aimed at disrupting President Joe Biden's interview on Late Night with Seth Meyers. In February 2025, through an eight-minute TikTok video, she criticized the Trump administration and the U.S. Department of State for changing her passport gender marker from female to male without her consent, stating it was important to track national developments and that it was a "good, necessary point" to share. Marcy Rheintgen, the first person arrested under Florida's anti-trans bathroom law, described Schafer as a personal hero who inspired her to challenge the law after receiving a male passport.
